thread:
Luca: Starting a thread — planned maintenance for runtime v2.3.1 tomorrow 02:00-03:30 UTC. Need comms for statuspage + cust email.
Priya: SGTM. Are we pinning dedicated customers to v2.2.x during the window?
Luca: Yes — for any Dedicated pools with >1TB KV usage we should pin to v2.2.9 for the window. Rollout plan: canary on 3 hosts, then 25%, 50%, 100% if green.
Sam: DeployBot reports last canary yesterday failed one node due to OOM on long-context job. We fixed the memory cap but want an extra night of testing.
DeployBot: deploy/2439156701 canary -> FAILED on host gpu-07 (OOM). See logs: `killed kernel: kv-cache allocate 1.8GB`
Luca: Thanks. That OOM fix is in 2.3.1-rc2. Because we need more test coverage, recommend: postpone full rollout 12 hours and run extended canary with traffic replay.
Priya: If we postpone, CustomerOps needs a revised statuspage message and email saying "extended maintenance window". Also list the affected customer tiers and mitigations (pinning + fallback to region B).
Alex: Drafted a short statuspage blurb — leaving here so we can iterate: 
```
Scheduled maintenance: 2026-04-08 02:00–04:00 UTC (extended)
We will be deploying runtime v2.3.1 to improve memory handling for long-context workloads. During the maintenance window some requests may experience higher latency or transient errors. Customers on Dedicated plans may be temporarily pinned to v2.2.9 to avoid disruptions. We expect full service to resume by 04:00 UTC.
Affected services: hosted API (may see degradation), Dedicated pools (possible pinning), Console UI (read-only for a short period). For real-time updates see status.redwood.ai/incident/RI-2026-041.
```
Priya: That looks fine; tighten the ETA and add fallback instructions for platform teams: who to ping and the runbook link.
Alex: Updated: added support contacts + runbook link, and changed time to 02:00–04:30 UTC.
CustomerOps: Can we include an optional opt-out line for top-tier enterprise customers who want to coordinate a bespoke window?
Luca: Yes — include: "Enterprises: contact your account manager to request a coordinated maintenance window or opt-out of automatic pinning."
Priya: We also need an email template that Support can ship to customers affected by pinning. Draft below — please review: 
```
Subject: Notice: Maintenance and temporary version pinning on April 8
Hi <CustomerName>,
We are performing scheduled maintenance to deploy runtime improvements that address memory issues for long-context workloads. To reduce risk, we will temporarily pin Dedicated pools to v2.2.9 during the window. What to expect:
- Window: Apr 8, 02:00–04:30 UTC
- Impact: Slight latency increase for some requests; no expected data loss. If you run long-context streaming jobs, consider reducing max_context for the window.
- Actions we are taking: temporary pinning, fallback routing to alternate region if needed, extended canary testing before full rollout.
If you need to opt out or coordinate a specific time, reply to this email or contact your account manager.
Thanks,
Redwood Support
```
Sam: A couple of ops notes: add a rollback trigger — if error rate >1.5% for 15m or P95 latency increase >200ms vs baseline, we rollback and notify. Also mark rolling deploy as manual pause at 25% to validate metrics.
Luca: Agreed — include metrics and who will approve rollback (Eng oncall + Product ops).
DeployBot: roll/status -> queued for extended canary at 23:30 UTC with traffic replay tag `longctx-replay`.
Priya: Final ask: statuspage should include a pinned line about "no auth changes" and confirm keys remain valid. Add that and we're good to publish.
Alex: Done. I'm going to publish draft to staging statuspage and queue the customer email batch for 01:00 UTC (so it's received before the window).
CustomerOps: We'll review enterprise list and send tailored outreach for 8 customers that require scheduling.
Luca: Thanks team. Action items: Alex publish draft -> 23:50 UTC, Sam start extended canary -> 23:30 UTC, Priya coordinate enterprise opt-outs, DeployBot will post updates in this thread.
DeployBot: update -> canary started on hosts gpu-03,gpu-05,gpu-09 at 23:30 UTC. Tracking metrics in #kpi-stream.
